quizName: Hardest Questions in Nebraska Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: When traveling at night, is it easy to judge distances?

options.text: Yes, it is easier than during the day.
It is about the same as during the day.
No, it is harder than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is harder than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances when driving at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lights can distort or hide these shadows and contrasts.

questions.question: How does improper braking affect motorcycle safety?

options.text: It usually causes no problems.
It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
It is not a concern since motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning the right braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What is the best reason to wear special clothing while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It feels comfortable.
It protects you if you crash.
It does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash. It also keeps you comfortable and makes sure other drivers can see you.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, it should:

options.text: Fit snugly.
Be clean.
Look cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it fits snugly all the way around, meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, and has no damage.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding?

options.text: Bright colors.
Dark colors.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to help other drivers see you, even during the day. Reflective materials on your clothing also help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What should you know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are not a concern.
You should check them before changing lanes.
They do not exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check them before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make this a habit.

questions.question: What should you do if you ride on a slippery surface?

options.text: Slow down
Speed up
Make sudden moves

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes gently when stopping.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue while riding?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take rest breaks often.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks often.
questions.explanation: Taking breaks during long rides helps reduce fatigue. Caffeine can make fatigue worse later when it wears off. Bad weather also increases fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield for long trips.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do first?

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it on the highway right away.
Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, find out where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on roads.

questions.question: How do reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing help motorcycle riders?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They help other drivers see you better.
They do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: How it looks
How well it protects your head
How much it costs

questions.correctAnswerText: How well it protects your head
questions.explanation: Protection is most important. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you wear?

options.text: Always wear a jacket.
Wear a jacket only at night.
Wear a jacket only when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, no matter what the weather is.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when merging into traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Keep safe distances between each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Do not worry about the distance between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe distances between each other.
questions.explanation: Ride in a staggered formation. This allows riders to stay together while keeping safe distances from each other.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-compliant helmet?

options.text: It will severely limit your side vision.
It will let you see adequately to both sides.
It will prevent you from turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will let you see adequately to both sides.
questions.explanation: DOT-approved helmets allow you to see clearly to the sides. The idea that helmets restrict vision is not true.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most to you?

options.text: The price.
The protection it offers.
How it looks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The protection it offers.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What can increase your chances of surviving a crash?

options.text: Wearing a DOT-compliant helmet.
Wearing a baseball cap.
Wearing comfortable shoes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a DOT-compliant helmet.
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet that meets DOT and state standards provides the best head and neck protection. Wearing a properly fitted and secured helmet is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This white sign with red and black markings tells drivers the traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Speed up.
Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Always check your brakes before riding. Test both brake controls to make sure each one lights up the brake lights.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body fast. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your body.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely and go only when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection:

options.text: To see if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
To watch for pedestrians ahead.
To look for dark clouds that show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to watch for vehicles behind you. This helps you see if drivers are paying attention to you and reacting to your actions.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually safe because over-the-counter medications are weak.
Is always acceptable.
Can affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medications, can make it harder to ride safely. Always ask your doctor how a new medication might affect your riding.
